    raw_token = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(40)
    invitation = account.invitations.new(
      invited_by: invited_by,
      email: email,
      role: role,
      token_digest: digest(raw_token),
      expires_at: TTL.from_now
    )

    account.with_lock do
      valid = invitation.valid?
      if invitation.email.present? && !invitation.errors.include?(:email)
        if account.users.exists?(email: invitation.email) || account.invitations.pending.exists?(email: invitation.email)
          invitation.errors.add(:email, :taken)
          valid = false
        end
      end
      raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(invitation) unless valid

      invitation.save!
    end

    UserMailer.invitation(invitation, raw_token).deliver_now

    invitation
  end

  def self.accept_for_account!(account:, raw_token:, name:, password:)
    return nil unless account && raw_token.is_a?(String) && raw_token.present?

    account.with_lock do
      invitation = account.invitations.pending.find_by(token_digest: digest(raw_token))

        role: invitation.role,
        verified: true,

      user
    end
  end

  def status(now = Time.current)

  end

  end

    raw_token = SecureRandom.alphanumeric(40)

    account.with_lock do

      if accepted?
        errors.add(:base, "Invitation has already been accepted")
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      if revoked?

      end

      end

        raise ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.new(self)
      end

      update!(revoked_at: Time.current)
    end

    self

If `{ page: { size: 25, after: nil } }` comes in, `after` is `nil` – and that makes sense for initial page load. But if *only* `after: nil` is sent, and *no* `size`, that should trigger the validation error. In fact, if all values in `page_params` are `nil`, we'll correctly get the `422` error. The same applies for `{ page: { after: "" } }`. It looks like we cover both cases!

Let's do some quick tests to solidify this. I'll test all combinations: with `size` and `after`, `after: nil`, `size: nil`, `size: ""`, `after: ""`, `before: ""`, and `before: nil` to make sure we're on the right track. This seems to be rock-solid!

And, before I go, let's look at `normalized_cursor_path`. The `.sub(/\.json\z/i, "").chomp("/")` is *elegant* because it cleans the URI path by ignoring trailing slashes and common extensions. Clients can hit `/api/v1/tickets` or `/api/v1/tickets.json` or `/api/v1/tickets/` all return the same results. `/api/v1/tickets` is distinct from `/api/v1/requests` or `/api/v1/tickets/1/comments`, as it should be.

Okay, I'm ready. I'll write `app/controllers/concerns/cursor_pagination.rb` and update `app/controllers/api/v1/base_controller.rb`.

require "base64"
require "json"
require "openssl"

module CursorPagination
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  class InvalidPaginationError < StandardError
    attr_reader :errors

    def initialize(message, errors = {})
      super(message)
      @errors = errors
    end
  end

  ALLOWED_CURSOR_PAGE_KEYS = %w[size after before].freeze
  CURSOR_SIGNATURE_BYTES = 16
  CURSOR_TOKEN_PATTERN = /\A[A-Za-z0-9\-_]+=*\z/
  MIN_TIMESTAMP_USEC = -62_135_596_800_000_000
  MAX_TIMESTAMP_USEC = 253_402_300_799_999_999

  private

  def paginate(scope, resource_key:, &serializer)
    if params[:page].is_a?(ActionController::Parameters)
      paginate_with_cursor(scope, resource_key: resource_key, &serializer)
    else
      paginate_with_offset(scope, resource_key: resource_key, &serializer)
    end
  end

  def paginate_with_offset(scope, resource_key:, &serializer)
    page = parse_pagination_param(params[:page], default: self.class::DEFAULT_PAGE, max: self.class::MAX_PAGE)
    per_page = parse_pagination_param(params[:per_page], default: self.class::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE, max: self.class::MAX_PER_PAGE)
    total_count = scope.count
    offset = (page - 1) * per_page

    records = if offset >= total_count
      []
    else
      scope.offset(offset).limit(per_page).map(&serializer)
    end

    {
      resource_key => records,
      count: total_count,
      page: page,
      per_page: per_page,
      next_page: (page * per_page < total_count) ? page + 1 : nil,
      previous_page: page > 1 ? page - 1 : nil
    }
  end

  def paginate_with_cursor(scope, resource_key:, &serializer)
    size, raw_after, raw_before = parse_cursor_page_params!
    order_columns = extract_order_columns!(scope)
    primary_direction = order_columns.first[1]
    after_op = (primary_direction == :desc) ? "<" : ">"
    before_op = (primary_direction == :desc) ? ">" : "<"

    if raw_after
      cursor_vals = decode_cursor!(raw_after, order_columns)
      fetched = apply_keyset_condition(scope, order_columns, after_op, cursor_vals).limit(size + 1).to_a
      has_next = fetched.length > size
      records = fetched.first(size)
      has_more = has_next
      has_prev = if records.empty?
        false
      else
        first_vals = extract_typed_order_values(records.first, order_columns)
        existence_scope = scope.except(:includes, :preload, :eager_load)
        apply_keyset_condition(existence_scope, order_columns, before_op, first_vals)
          .reorder(build_inverted_arel_orderings(scope, order_columns))
          .exists?
      end
    elsif raw_before
      cursor_vals = decode_cursor!(raw_before, order_columns)
      fetched = apply_keyset_condition(scope, order_columns, before_op, cursor_vals)
        .reorder(build_inverted_arel_orderings(scope, order_columns))
        .limit(size + 1)
        .to_a
      has_prev = fetched.length > size
      records = fetched.first(size).reverse
      has_more = has_prev
      has_next = if records.empty?
        false
      else
        last_vals = extract_typed_order_values(records.last, order_columns)
        existence_scope = scope.except(:includes, :preload, :eager_load)
        apply_keyset_condition(existence_scope, order_columns, after_op, last_vals).exists?
      end
    else
      fetched = scope.limit(size + 1).to_a
      has_next = fetched.length > size
      records = fetched.first(size)
      has_prev = false
      has_more = has_next
    end

    if records.empty?
      before_cursor = nil
      after_cursor = nil
      next_link = nil
      prev_link = nil
    else
      before_cursor = encode_cursor(records.first, order_columns)
      after_cursor = encode_cursor(records.last, order_columns)
      next_link = has_next ? build_cursor_link(direction: :after, cursor: after_cursor, size: size) : nil
      prev_link = has_prev ? build_cursor_link(direction: :before, cursor: before_cursor, size: size) : nil
    end

    {
      resource_key => records.map(&serializer),
      meta: {
        has_more: has_more,
        after_cursor: after_cursor,
        before_cursor: before_cursor
      },
      links: {
        next: next_link,
        prev: prev_link
      }
    }
  end

  def parse_cursor_page_params!
    page_params = params[:page]
    raw_hash = page_params.to_unsafe_h
    keys = raw_hash.keys.map(&:to_s)

    if keys.empty? || (keys - ALLOWED_CURSOR_PAGE_KEYS).any? || raw_hash.values.all?(&:nil?)
      raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Page parameters are invalid", { page: ["is invalid"] })
    end

    size = if raw_hash.key?("size") && !raw_hash["size"].nil?
      parse_cursor_size!(raw_hash["size"])
    else
      self.class::DEFAULT_PER_PAGE
    end

    raw_after = if raw_hash.key?("after") && !raw_hash["after"].nil?
      parse_raw_cursor_string!(raw_hash["after"], :after)
    end

    raw_before = if raw_hash.key?("before") && !raw_hash["before"].nil?
      parse_raw_cursor_string!(raw_hash["before"], :before)
    end

    if raw_after && raw_before
      raise InvalidPaginationError.new(
        "Cannot specify both page[after] and page[before]",
        { page: ["cannot specify both after and before"] }
      )
    end

    [size, raw_after, raw_before]
  end

  def parse_cursor_size!(raw_size)
    parsed = if raw_size.is_a?(String)
      stripped = raw_size.strip
      stripped.to_i if /\A\d+\z/.match?(stripped)
    elsif raw_size.is_a?(Integer)
      raw_size
    end

    unless parsed && parsed >= 1
      raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Page size is invalid", { "page.size": ["must be a positive integer"] })
    end

    [parsed, self.class::MAX_PER_PAGE].min
  end

  def parse_raw_cursor_string!(raw_value, key)
    unless raw_value.is_a?(String) && !raw_value.empty? && raw_value.bytesize.between?(20, 1024) && CURSOR_TOKEN_PATTERN.match?(raw_value)
      raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Invalid cursor", { "page.#{key}": ["is invalid"] })
    end

    raw_value
  end

  def extract_order_columns!(scope)
    orderings = scope.order_values
    if orderings.empty?
      orderings = [scope.klass.arel_table[:id].asc]
    end

    columns = orderings.map do |ordering|
      col_name = ordering.expr.name.to_s
      direction = ordering.direction
      col_meta = scope.klass.columns_hash.fetch(col_name)
      [col_name, direction, col_meta.type]
    end

    directions = columns.map { |_, dir, _| dir }.uniq
    if directions.length != 1
      raise ArgumentError, "Mixed cursor sort directions are not supported: #{columns.inspect}"
    end

    columns
  end

  def build_inverted_arel_orderings(scope, order_columns)
    arel_table = scope.klass.arel_table
    order_columns.map do |col_name, direction, _col_type|
      (direction == :desc) ? arel_table[col_name].asc : arel_table[col_name].desc
    end
  end

  def apply_keyset_condition(scope, order_columns, operator, typed_values)
    conn = scope.klass.connection
    quoted_table = conn.quote_table_name(scope.klass.table_name)

    if order_columns.length == 1
      col_name = order_columns.first[0]
      quoted_col = "#{quoted_table}.#{conn.quote_column_name(col_name)}"
      scope.where("#{quoted_col} #{operator} ?", typed_values.first)
    else
      quoted_cols = order_columns.map do |col_name, _, _|
        "#{quoted_table}.#{conn.quote_column_name(col_name)}"
      end.join(", ")
      placeholders = Array.new(order_columns.length, "?").join(", ")
      scope.where("(#{quoted_cols}) #{operator} (#{placeholders})", *typed_values)
    end
  end

  def extract_typed_order_values(record, order_columns)
    order_columns.map do |col_name, _dir, col_type|
      val = record.public_send(col_name)
      case col_type
      when :datetime
        val.utc
      when :integer
        val.to_i
      else
        val
      end
    end
  end

  def encode_cursor(record, order_columns)
    serialized_values = order_columns.map do |col_name, _dir, col_type|
      val = record.public_send(col_name)
      case col_type
      when :datetime
        t = val.utc
        t.tv_sec * 1_000_000 + t.usec
      when :integer
        val.to_i
      else
        val
      end
    end

    payload_json = JSON.generate({
      a: current_account.id,
      p: normalized_cursor_path,
      k: serialized_values
    })
    sig = OpenSSL::HMAC.digest("SHA256", cursor_signing_key, payload_json).byteslice(0, CURSOR_SIGNATURE_BYTES)
    Base64.urlsafe_encode64(sig + payload_json, padding: false)
  end

  def decode_cursor!(raw_cursor, order_columns)
    decoded = Base64.urlsafe_decode64(raw_cursor)
    if decoded.bytesize <= CURSOR_SIGNATURE_BYTES
      raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Invalid cursor", { cursor: ["is invalid"] })
    end

    sig = decoded.byteslice(0, CURSOR_SIGNATURE_BYTES)
    payload_json = decoded.byteslice(CURSOR_SIGNATURE_BYTES..-1)
    expected_sig = OpenSSL::HMAC.digest("SHA256", cursor_signing_key, payload_json).byteslice(0, CURSOR_SIGNATURE_BYTES)

    unless ActiveSupport::SecurityUtils.secure_compare(sig, expected_sig)
      raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Invalid cursor", { cursor: ["is invalid"] })
    end

    data = JSON.parse(payload_json)
    unless data.is_a?(Hash) &&
        data["a"] == current_account.id &&
        data["p"] == normalized_cursor_path &&
        data["k"].is_a?(Array) &&
        data["k"].length == order_columns.length
      raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Invalid cursor", { cursor: ["is invalid"] })
    end

    order_columns.each_with_index.map do |(_col_name, _dir, col_type), idx|
      raw_val = data["k"][idx]
      case col_type
      when :datetime
        unless raw_val.is_a?(Integer) && raw_val.between?(MIN_TIMESTAMP_USEC, MAX_TIMESTAMP_USEC)
          raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Invalid cursor", { cursor: ["is invalid"] })
        end
        Time.at(raw_val.div(1_000_000), raw_val.modulo(1_000_000), :usec, in: "UTC")
      when :integer
        unless raw_val.is_a?(Integer) && raw_val.between?(1, self.class::MAX_BIGINT)
          raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Invalid cursor", { cursor: ["is invalid"] })
        end
        raw_val
      else
        raw_val
      end
    end
  rescue ArgumentError, JSON::ParserError
    raise InvalidPaginationError.new("Invalid cursor", { cursor: ["is invalid"] })
  end

  def build_cursor_link(direction:, cursor:, size:)
    query_params = request.query_parameters.deep_dup
    query_params.delete("per_page")
    page_hash = { "size" => size.to_s }
    page_hash[direction.to_s] = cursor
    query_params["page"] = page_hash

    "#{request.base_url}#{request.path}?#{query_params.to_query}"
  end

  def normalized_cursor_path
    path = request.path.to_s.sub(/\.json\z/i, "").chomp("/")
    path.empty? ? "/" : path
  end

  def cursor_signing_key
    "helpdesk_cursor_v1:#{Rails.application.secret_key_base}"
  end

  def render_invalid_pagination(exception)
    render json: {
      error: exception.message,
      errors: exception.errors
    }, status: :unprocessable_content
  end
end
EOF

steps.message: I will run the live Puma HTTP cursor pagination test using `Session.issue_for!(admin).token`.
steps.reasoning_content:
Here's your summary:

**The Eureka Moment & Immediate Validation**

Aha! That's it! I've got it, `Session.issue_for!(admin).token`! That's the key to unlocking the functionality I've been aiming for. Now, let's not waste any time theorizing – I need to see this work in real time. I'm going to kick off that live Puma HTTP test right now. No more dry runs; let's put this code through its paces and confirm its behavior under actual conditions. I need to validate this immediately!

arguments.command:
cd /app && RAILS_ENV=test bin/rails runner '
require "net/http"
require "json"
require "uri"

env = { "RAILS_ENV" => "test", "ACTION_MAILER_DELIVERY_METHOD" => "test" }
pid = spawn(env, "bin/rails", "server", "-p", "13579", "-b", "127.0.0.1", out: "/tmp/puma_test.log", err: "/tmp/puma_test.log")

begin
  30.times do
    res = Net::HTTP.get_response(URI("http://127.0.0.1:13579/up"))
    break if res.code == "200"
  rescue Errno::ECONNREFUSED
    sleep 0.2
  end

  Account.where(subdomain: "pumatest").destroy_all
  acc = Account.create!(name: "Puma Co", subdomain: "pumatest")
  admin = acc.users.create!(name: "Admin", email: "admin@pumatest.test", password: "secret123", role: "admin", verified: true, email_verified_at: Time.current)
  acc.update!(owner: admin)
  cust = acc.users.create!(name: "Cust", email: "cust@pumatest.test", password: "secret123", role: "customer", verified: true, email_verified_at: Time.current)
  raw_tok = Session.issue_for!(admin).token

  headers = { "X-Helpdesk-Account" => "pumatest", "Authorization" => "Bearer #{raw_tok}" }

  uri = URI("http://127.0.0.1:13579/api/v1/tickets?page[size]=25&status=open")
  res = Net::HTTP.start(uri.hostname, uri.port) { |h| h.request(Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri, headers)) }
  puts "Empty response (#{res.code}): #{res.body}"
  expected_empty = "{\"tickets\":[],\"meta\":{\"has_more\":false,\"after_cursor\":null,\"before_cursor\":null},\"links\":{\"next\":null,\"prev\":null}}"
  raise "Unexpected empty body: #{res.body}" unless res.body == expected_empty

  5.times do |i|
    t = Time.utc(2026, 11, 20, 15, 0, i)
    Ticket.create!(account: acc, requester: cust, subject: "T#{i + 1}", status: "open", priority: "normal", created_at: t, updated_at: t, customer_updated_at: t)
  end

  uri1 = URI("http://127.0.0.1:13579/api/v1/tickets?page[size]=2&status=open")
  res1 = Net::HTTP.start(uri1.hostname, uri1.port) { |h| h.request(Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri1, headers)) }
  b1 = JSON.parse(res1.body)
  raise "Page 1 mismatch" unless b1["tickets"].map { |t| t["subject"] } == ["T5", "T4"] && b1["meta"]["has_more"] == true && b1["links"]["prev"].nil?

  uri2 = URI(b1["links"]["next"])
  res2 = Net::HTTP.start(uri2.hostname, uri2.port) { |h| h.request(Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri2, headers)) }
  b2 = JSON.parse(res2.body)
  raise "Page 2 mismatch" unless b2["tickets"].map { |t| t["subject"] } == ["T3", "T2"] && b2["meta"]["has_more"] == true

  uri3 = URI(b2["links"]["next"])
  res3 = Net::HTTP.start(uri3.hostname, uri3.port) { |h| h.request(Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri3, headers)) }
  b3 = JSON.parse(res3.body)
  raise "Page 3 mismatch" unless b3["tickets"].map { |t| t["subject"] } == ["T1"] && b3["meta"]["has_more"] == false && b3["links"]["next"].nil?

  uri_prev2 = URI(b3["links"]["prev"])
  res_prev2 = Net::HTTP.start(uri_prev2.hostname, uri_prev2.port) { |h| h.request(Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri_prev2, headers)) }
  bp2 = JSON.parse(res_prev2.body)
  raise "Prev 2 mismatch" unless bp2["tickets"].map { |t| t["subject"] } == ["T3", "T2"] && bp2["meta"]["has_more"] == true

  uri_prev1 = URI(bp2["links"]["prev"])
  res_prev1 = Net::HTTP.start(uri_prev1.hostname, uri_prev1.port) { |h| h.request(Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri_prev1, headers)) }
  bp1 = JSON.parse(res_prev1.body)
  raise "Prev 1 mismatch" unless bp1["tickets"].map { |t| t["subject"] } == ["T5", "T4"] && bp1["meta"]["has_more"] == false && bp1["links"]["prev"].nil?

  puts "Live Puma HTTP cursor pagination test passed 100%!"
ensure
  Account.where(subdomain: "pumatest").destroy_all rescue nil
  Process.kill("TERM", pid) rescue nil
  Process.wait(pid) rescue nil
  File.delete("/tmp/puma_test.log") if File.exist?("/tmp/puma_test.log")
end
'

steps.message:
Cursor pagination has been implemented across all collection endpoints while preserving full compatibility with the existing page-number API:

- **Cursor Pagination Concern (`app/controllers/concerns/cursor_pagination.rb`) & BaseController Integration (`app/controllers/api/v1/base_controller.rb`)**:
  - Supports `page[size]`, `page[after]`, and `page[before]` on all 9 collection endpoints (`/api/v1/tickets`, `/api/v1/tickets/:ticket_id/comments`, `/api/v1/requests`, `/api/v1/requests/:request_id/comments`, `/api/v1/users`, `/api/v1/staff`, `/api/v1/groups`, `/api/v1/group_memberships`, and `/api/v1/invitations`) while keeping existing `page` / `per_page` offset pagination untouched.
  - Uses keyset tuple comparisons (`ROW(...) < ROW(...)` / `ROW(...) > ROW(...)`) with `LIMIT (size + 1)` and zero `COUNT(*)` or `OFFSET` queries so deep browsing stays constant-time.
  - Encodes HMAC-signed, account- and endpoint-scoped snapshot cursors containing microsecond timestamps and primary-key tiebreakers (`before_cursor` for the first record, `after_cursor` for the last record) so navigation stays stable even when concurrent users create, reply to, update, close, or delete records.
  - Returns `meta` (`has_more` in the active browsing direction, `after_cursor`, `before_cursor`) and `links` (`next`, `prev` preserving active query filters) and rejects malformed, conflicting, tampered, or cross-scope cursors with `422 Unprocessable Content`.
- **Database Indexes (`db/migrate/20261120200000_add_cursor_pagination_indexes.rb`)**:
  - Added composite B-tree indexes across `tickets`, `comments`, and `users` so filtered and unfiltered keyset queries execute via index scans without sorting.
- **Integration Tests (`test/integration/cursor_pagination_test.rb`)**:
  - Verified empty/populated cursor payloads, forward/backward navigation via `links` and explicit `page[after]`/`page[before]` across all 9 collections, concurrent mutation stability, validation/security checks, and SQL index scan behavior.

I will now submit the final output.
